Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team is validating providers on the SIG/CAIQ and had two questions about log retention for a specific integration we plan to run in prod. The integration ingests identifiable telemetry from user devices and our legal team requires a 180-day preservation window for certain forensic cases (rather than Redwood's default 90-day ephemeral logs).

Can you confirm: 
- Whether Redwood supports customer-specific log-retention overrides per account or project, and how that is implemented (config vs. policy).
- What evidence you can provide for the SIG/CAIQ question A.2.x (log retention and deletion controls) to show an exception is in place and auditable.
- If you can share a redacted sample of the audit/export showing a 180-day retention flag for a test tenant, that would help our SOC team.

We need to close this in our security review by next Friday (May 29). Appreciate any attachments or links you can provide.

Best,

- Evidence: we can provide a completed SIG matrix with callouts for retention controls, a signed exception form (policy change request), and a redacted audit export showing the applied retention window for a sandbox tenant.
- Sample: attaching a small CSV with masked identifiers that shows retention_window_days=180 for the sample tenant row.

Attached for your review: redwood_sig_matrix_v1.3.xlsx (highlighted A.2.x), sample-audit-logs-hr-zone.csv, and a PDF retention-exception form that we use for legal/ops signoff.

Hey Alex — quick technical note to supplement Dylan's attachments.

How it works (high-level):
- Retention is implemented as an account-level policy record stored in our control plane; it is bound to the account ID and enforced by the serving runtime when logs are written/evicted.
- We persist a retention metadata token (hashed policy id, retention_window_days) in the log index; evictions are performed by a background retention worker that checks policy TTL.
- For customers requiring longer preservation (180d in your case) we create a signed exception directive that is visible in the audit log (operation: retention.policy.update, actor: compliance@redwoodinference.com).

I exported a redacted sample of the audit log for a sandbox tenant (attached) — the CSV shows the policy update entry and the applied retention_window_days column set to 180. Fields with PII are masked.

If Horizon needs a SYSLOG or SIEM-friendly feed of these audit events, we can also enable a one-way push to your Splunk/LogRhythm instance for the duration of the engagement (we've done this for other customers under an NDA).

Regards,
Marcus Lin

Redwood Inference
